reports.title: Thomas Green
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths
Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: It was unclear why a referral was made to Adult General Psychiatry whilst Mr Green remained an inpatient, there was no evidence that this referral was ever considered or actioned.
concerns.hazard: referral to adult general psychiatry while inpatient not considered or acted upon

concerns.quote: when Mr Green was discharged from hospital there was no psychiatric follow-up and no treatment plan in place to address the diagnosis of complex PTSD. 3
concerns.hazard: discharge without psychiatric follow-up or treatment plan for complex PTSD

concerns.quote: The Court heard evidence how this was not a case which was suitable for Healthy Minds as it was complex and involved potentially complex PTSD.
concerns.hazard: inappropriate referral to Healthy Minds for complex PTSD case

concerns.quote: The Court heard evidence that the referral document completed by the GP was not particularly detailed and therefore the complexity of the case was not apparent and the case was accepted.
concerns.hazard: inadequate GP referral failing to convey complexity

concerns.quote: The Court heard evidence that there is a commissioning gap for the provision of services for Complex PTSD and complex presentations such as that of Mr Green.
concerns.hazard: lack of commissioned services for complex PTSD

reports.title: John Haines
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The CCG commissioned a new Primary Care Mental Health Pathway during 2016/17, which mobilised in May 2017. The model has been developed to respond to the local population needs, preparing service users to access therapy in order to optimise recovery performance. The service is subject to robust a performance dependent payment framework which provides assurance of performance delivery.
promises.summary: Commissioned Primary Care Mental Health Pathway to improve therapy access

concerns.quote: During the course of the evidence it became apparent that mental health in-patients still do not have access to therapy from a qualified Psychologist, despite the fact that this has been raised in previous Regulation 28 PFD Forms. Notably, all clinicians were of the professional view that psychological therapy was critical to treatment, alongside psychiatric care.
concerns.hazard: lack of access to qualified psychologist for mental health in-patients

concerns.quote: Similarly, patients cannot access a qualified Psychologist whilst under the care of the Home Treatment Team (HTT') etc. The only way for patients to get access to a Psychologist is through referral to 'Healthy Minds'. Health Minds cannot provide access where the patient remains under the care of the HTT etc.
concerns.hazard: lack of access to qualified psychologist while under Home Treatment Team care

concerns.quote: Timely access to Healthy Minds is also hindered by long waiting times.
concerns.hazard: long waiting times for Healthy Minds access

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that patients cannot obtain appropriate psychological support through Healthy Minds while under other care pathways. The earlier case concerned an unsuitable referral for complex PTSD; the later case notes a general lack of psychologist access for Home Treatment Team patients.
links.earlier_quote: When a referral was made this was made to Healthy Minds. The Court heard evidence how this was not a case which was suitable for Healthy Minds as it was complex and involved potentially complex PTSD.
links.later_quote: Similarly, patients cannot access a qualified Psychologist whilst under the care of the Home Treatment Team (HTT') etc. The only way for patients to get access to a Psychologist is through referral to 'Healthy Minds'. Health Minds cannot provide access where the patient remains under the care of the HTT etc.
links.promise_quote: The CCG will clarify the Individual Funding Request process to ensure that, where required, Pennine Care staff can apply for individual funding for extraordinary care, e.g. for Complex PTSD and ensure that PC.FT staff are fully briefed about the process by 1/6/17.

followups.summary: The organisation did not state that the pathway was commissioned or operational by May 2017.
